nodes.body: `atomic_count` only increments for `nir_intrinsic_ssbo_atomic`, but NIR also has other SSBO atomic intrinsics (e.g. `nir_intrinsic_ssbo_atomic_swap`). Since this detector’s contract is “no atomic”, it should treat those as atomics too; otherwise a shader with an atomic swap could be misdetected as a multitap gather.

`input_ssbo_binding` is taken from the first `load_ssbo` found while scanning the whole shader, but the detector doesn’t ensure that this load is actually one of the add-tree tap leaves. If there are extra `load_ssbo` instructions (even if the store value is still a pure add-tree), the recorded input binding can be wrong and the shape may not be representable by the planned lowering. A simple way to avoid false positives here is to require that the number of `load_ssbo` intrinsics equals the number of tap leaves in the reduction tree.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject stores under conditionals**

When the only `store_ssbo` is inside a `nir_if`, this detector still accepts it because the ancestor walk only records loops. A predicated convolution such as `if (mask[gid]) out[gid] = in[gid-1] + in[gid] + in[gid+1]` then matches the multitap shape, but the documented lowering is an unconditional multi-TEX draw, so masked-off pixels would be overwritten instead of preserving the predicate semantics. Please track `nir_cf_node_if` for the store, as the predicated-store detector does, and reject or route that shape separately.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject mixed-input tap trees**

If the add tree contains `load_ssbo` leaves from different bindings, for example `out = a[i-1] + b[i] + c[i+1]`, this helper counts all of them as taps and the detector later records only one `input_ssbo_binding`. Since the documented lowering uses one sampler for the gathered input, these mixed-buffer reductions are admitted as a single-input convolution and will sample the non-first inputs from the wrong buffer. Please carry/check each leaf's binding and reject anything except one gathered input binding.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-canonical tap offsets**

This acceptance point only proves that the stored value is a sum of at least three SSBO loads; it never checks that those loads use the canonical neighborhood offsets the lowering will synthesize. A same-buffer kernel such as `out[i] = in[i] + in[i + 16] + in[i + 32]` will therefore be classified as the box-kernel gather described in the comment and replayed with different sample coordinates, producing the wrong result. Please verify the leaf offsets match the supported kernel, or keep this detector false until arbitrary offsets are carried into the lowering.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject multi-row gather dispatches**

When `total_invocations > 2048`, `derive_raster_extent()` produces `width == 2048` and `height > 1`, but the synthesized gather FS only adds/subtracts `(1/width, 0)` and relies on CLAMP_TO_EDGE. In those multi-row dispatches, the right tap for element 2047 clamps to the last texel of row 0 instead of sampling element 2048 on row 1, and the left tap for each row start similarly clamps to itself, so every 2048-element boundary is silently computed with the wrong neighbors. Until the FS handles row carry, this path should reject `total_invocations > 2048` rather than accepting the full 2048x2048 extent.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor storage-buffer descriptor offsets**

For valid storage-buffer descriptors with a non-zero `VkDescriptorBufferInfo::offset`, `VkUpdateDescriptorSets` preserves that offset in `r300vk_descriptor.c`, but this replay maps `out_buf->resource` from byte 0 (and the input wrap above also uses `in_buf->resource` from byte 0). Such bindings will read the wrong input slice and overwrite the beginning of the VkBuffer instead of the descriptor's range, corrupting unrelated data in any app that suballocates multiple SSBOs from one buffer.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject conditional gather stores**

This new replay path also runs for multi-tap stores nested under a predicate: `r300_nir_detect_multitap_gather_pattern` only rejects loops and never checks the store's control-flow parent for `nir_if`, so a kernel like `if (pred) out[i] = in[i-1] + in[i] + in[i+1]` sets `is_multitap_gather`. The orchestrator then draws a full-screen quad with no predicate/discard handling, overwriting elements whose condition was false instead of leaving them unchanged, so the dispatch should either reject non-unconditional stores or lower the predicate explicitly before entering this branch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require gather taps to use one input binding**

The replay binds only the single sampler resolved from `pl->multitap_gather.input_ssbo_binding`, but the detector accepts any iadd tree whose leaves are `load_ssbo` and only records the first load's binding. For a valid kernel that sums three SSBOs (for example `out[i] = a[i] + b[i] + c[i]`), this branch still runs and samples all three taps from the first buffer, silently ignoring the other bound inputs. The lowering should reject mixed load bindings or carry each tap's binding through to separate sampler views before enabling the draw.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve 32-bit integer add semantics**

This wraps scalar SSBO words as `PIPE_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM`, so the fragment program performs four normalized byte-channel additions and writes a clamped RGBA8 result. For accepted gather kernels whose taps produce a byte carry or any channel sum above 255, Vulkan/NIR `iadd` should produce a 32-bit integer result, but this path produces a bytewise saturating result instead; the detector has no value-range guard, so ordinary inputs outside the probe's <=85-per-byte envelope are silently miscomputed.

nodes.body: The MapMemory block comment says BindBufferMemory2 will make the VkBuffer reference the same resource (no copy), but the implementation below actually copies into buf->resource. This is misleading, especially since it affects coherency expectations for map-after-bind.

owns_buffer is set when MapMemory lazily creates a buffer backing. But later in MapMemory (PIPE_BUFFER path) the code always treats mem->memory_offset as the base of the bound resource (offset < memory_offset check + offset - memory_offset). After a bind with non-zero memoryOffset, that makes mapping offsets incorrect for owns_buffer allocations (resource represents the whole VkDeviceMemory).

BindBufferMemory2 unmaps mem->transfer when owns_buffer is set. If the application still considers the VkDeviceMemory mapped (legal in Vulkan), this invalidates the pointer returned by vkMapMemory and makes a later vkUnmapMemory a no-op, breaking Vulkan's mapping lifetime guarantees.

This copy path assumes memoryOffset is within the VkDeviceMemory allocation. If memoryOffset > mem->size, `mem->size - memoryOffset` underflows and the subsequent u_box_1d/ buffer_map can read out of bounds. Please range-check (memoryOffset + buf->size <= mem->size) before computing `avail`/`copy_bytes`.

With lazy map-before-bind (owns_buffer), BindImageMemory2 can now be called while mem->resource is the lazily-created PIPE_BUFFER and/or while mem->transfer is live. The current BindImageMemory2 (below) will replace mem->resource without unmapping, risking UAF on the mapped transfer, and it also leaves owns_buffer true even after switching the resource to a texture.

**suggestion (performance):** Avoid direct `getenv` in the hot path and rely on Mesa helpers / caching instead.

Calling `getenv` on every `r300_is_format_supported` call adds avoidable overhead and bypasses Mesa’s usual config/option handling. Instead, read this option once at screen initialization via a helper like `debug_get_bool_option`, store the result in the screen struct (e.g. `screen->ati2n_experimental`), and reference that cached flag here. This preserves behavior while avoiding repeated environment lookups and matches existing Mesa patterns for driver options.

Suggested implementation:

```c
#include "util/u_format.h"
#include "util/u_debug.h"

```

```c
struct r300_screen {
    bool ati2n_experimental;

```

```c
    rscreen = CALLOC_STRUCT(r300_screen);

    /* Cache R300_EXPERIMENTAL_ATI2N at screen creation time to avoid
     * getenv() in hot paths and to follow Mesa option handling
     * conventions. The default (false) keeps R300-class ATI2N disabled.
     */
    rscreen->ati2n_experimental =
        debug_get_bool_option("R300_EXPERIMENTAL_ATI2N", false);

```

```c
	 * disabled, so default behavior is unchanged.
	 *
	 * The R300_EXPERIMENTAL_ATI2N option is cached at screen creation time
	 * (rscreen->ati2n_experimental) to avoid getenv() in the hot path and
	 * to integrate with Mesa's option handling.
	 */
        (is_r500 ||
         (is_ati2n && rscreen->ati2n_experimental) ||
         !is_ati2n) &&
        r300_is_sampler_format_supported(format)) {
        retval |= PIPE_BIND_SAMPLER_VIEW;
    }

```

1. Ensure the `r300_screen` typedef/definition in this file actually uses the name `struct r300_screen` as in the SEARCH block; if it differs, adjust the SEARCH/REPLACE accordingly and keep the `bool ati2n_experimental;` member in that struct.
2. In the screen creation function, if the variable name is not `rscreen`, replace it accordingly when assigning `ati2n_experimental`.
3. If your codebase uses `boolean` instead of `bool` in `struct r300_screen`, change the added field to `boolean ati2n_experimental;` and use `FALSE` instead of `false` in `debug_get_bool_option`.
4. If `debug_get_bool_option` is already included via another header, you can omit the new `#include "util/u_debug.h"` line.

nodes.body: The comment calls this an “atomic swap”, but `pacman -U` isn’t atomic in the strict sense (it’s a transaction, but can still leave partial state on failure). Reword to avoid implying stronger guarantees than pacman provides.

Repo guidance discourages embedding local paths in source comments (AGENTS.md:400-404). This comment hard-codes `../../build/`; consider describing the build area in terms of the Make variables instead so the comment stays correct if the layout changes.

`deploy-mesa-gororoba` performs a non-interactive `pacman -U --overwrite '*'` on the remote host with `yes | ...`, which is intentionally destructive but also easy to run by accident. Add an explicit opt-in flag (e.g. `DEPLOY_FORCE=1`) so a mistyped make invocation can’t overwrite system files silently.

**suggestion:** Non-interactive `yes | sudo pacman --overwrite '*'` is quite heavy-handed and may hide failures

Piping `yes` into `sudo -n pacman -U --overwrite '*'` auto-accepts all prompts and overwrites any conflicting files, which is risky for a generic deployment one‑liner. If this is for CI/infra, consider using `--noconfirm` instead of `yes |` and restricting `--overwrite` to the specific Mesa paths rather than `'*'` to avoid clobbering unrelated files and make unexpected conflicts more visible.

Suggested implementation:

```
	scp "$$pkg" "$(TARGET_HOST):/tmp/" && \
	ssh "$(TARGET_HOST)" "sudo -n pacman -U --noconfirm \
		--overwrite /usr/lib/lib\*mesa\* \
		--overwrite /usr/lib/dri/\* \
		--overwrite /usr/share/drirc.d/\* \
		/tmp/$$(basename $$pkg)"

```

You may want to further tune the `--overwrite` globs to exactly match the files your `mesa-gororoba` package owns (e.g. by checking `pacman -Ql mesa-gororoba` on a test system) and remove any patterns that are not actually needed. If this Makefile is used on systems with different Mesa layouts (e.g. multilib or custom prefixes), you might also need to add or adjust paths accordingly.

nodes.body: This packet never programs the `NUM_VERTICES` field, so the draw count is zero. Existing `DRAW_VBUF_2` emitters include `(count << R300_VAP_VF_CNTL__NUM_VERTICES__SHIFT)` in `VAP_VF_CNTL`; without it, pass 1 will not emit the fragments needed to populate the R2VB buffer.

This `LOAD_VBPNTR` sequence is missing the reserved zero dword that `r300_emit_vertex_arrays_swtcl` emits between the offset and relocation for the same packet layout. Dropping that dword changes the packet body layout, so the relocation dwords can be parsed as payload instead of the BO relocation.

This second `DRAW_VBUF_2` also omits the `NUM_VERTICES` field, so the re-ingest pass would submit a zero-vertex draw. Match the existing r300 draw emitters by encoding `num_vertices` in `VAP_VF_CNTL`.
`R300_VAP_VF_MAX_VTX_INDX` is an inclusive maximum index; existing r300 emitters write `count - 1`. Writing `num_vertices` admits one vertex past the end of the FP32x4 stream.

These relocations are emitted without registering `output_gart_bo` in the command stream buffer list. Other r300 relocation users pair `OUT_CS_RELOC` with `cs_add_buffer`; without equivalent validation wiring, a live submit can fail CS validation because the relocation lookup has no registered BO entry.

This comment says the barrier is the same `cb_flush_clean` sequence, but the existing sequence also flushes `R300_ZB_ZCACHE_CTLSTAT` before `RADEON_WAIT_UNTIL`. Either emit the full barrier or narrow the comment so future callers do not mistake this subset for the driver’s verified full flush.

nodes.body: For the very chipsets this self-test targets (RS480/RS482, where `!caps.has_tcl`), `r300_buffer_create` allocates `PIPE_BIND_VERTEX_BUFFER` resources in CPU `malloced_buffer` memory and leaves `r300_resource->buf == NULL` (see `r300_screen_buffer.c:165-169`). The R2VB emitter immediately dereferences `output_gart_bo->buf` via `cs_add_buffer` and `cs_lookup_buffer` (`r300_r2vb.c:50`, `r300_r2vb.c:126`), so this `resource_create` path will hand the emitter a NULL BO and crash on the only hardware where the test is meant to run. The throwaway buffer needs to be allocated through a path that always yields a winsys BO in GTT — e.g. setting `PIPE_BIND_CUSTOM` (which bypasses the `!has_tcl` SWTCL-RAM branch) or calling `r300screen->rws->buffer_create` directly.

`r300_emit_rs482_r2vb_capture_selftest` is called unconditionally from `r300_create_context` whenever `R300_R2VB_TIMING` is set, with no chipset check. The emitter is RS482/RS480-specific (it relies on `R300_VAP_TCL_BYPASS` being set unconditionally for RS482, and on the absence of a real vertex shader). On any other r300/r400/r500 chipset, setting the env var will inject RS482-only packets into a fresh context's IB and either be rejected by the CS validator or — in submit mode — risk hanging non-target hardware. Please gate the self-test on the RS480 family (e.g. `r300->screen->caps.family == CHIP_RS480` plus `!caps.has_tcl`) before doing any work.

The emitter's documented contract (see comment at `r300_r2vb.c:69-76`) requires the caller to have already bound the "vertex compute" fragment program, the GTT framebuffer, and the pass-1 geometry through the normal pipe-state path, so that `r300_emit_dirty_state` has emitted the US instruction state, RS interpolator state, and GA/SU setup into the same IB. This self-test invokes the loop directly from `r300_create_context`, before any of that state has been bound or emitted — `dirty_hw` is zero and no FS/FB/VBO has been set. As a result, even "capture" mode produces a structurally incomplete IB (no US microcode, no RS/GA/SU, no PSC matching the FP32x4 stream), which defeats the stated purpose of validating the packet sequence; "submit" mode would feed garbage state to the validator/HW. The self-test needs to bind a minimal vertex-compute FS + GTT framebuffer + pass-1 VBO and force a dirty-state emit before calling `r300_emit_rs482_r2vb_compute_loop`, or the README/contract should be reconciled with what this harness actually exercises.

The submit path calls `r300->rws->cs_flush` directly instead of going through `r300_flush_and_cleanup` / the pipe's `flush` hook. That bypasses `r300_emit_hyperz_end`, `r300_emit_query_end`, the `flush_counter` bump, the `dirty_hw = 0` reset, and the per-atom re-dirty + `vertex_arrays_dirty = true` reset that the driver expects after every submission (`r300_flush.c:19-47`). Calling this from `r300_create_context` happens to leave the context in a clean-enough state to limp on, but using the winsys hook directly is a footgun if this self-test is ever moved or run more than once. Prefer `r300->context.flush(&r300->context, &fence, 0)` (capture mode can stay on the raw winsys hook since `RADEON_FLUSH_NOOP` is a winsys-level concept).

Any value of `R300_R2VB_TIMING` other than the exact string `"submit"` silently selects the capture path — including typos like `R300_R2VB_TIMING=Submit`, `submit\n`, `caputre`, `1`, `yes`, etc. Given that the difference between modes is "no hardware risk" vs. "raw submit that can hang the GPU", silently downgrading an unrecognized value to capture is the safe default, but please at least diagnose unknown values to stderr so a user who meant submit isn't misled into thinking they got a timed run when stderr says `r2vb_capture …`. Recommend explicitly checking for `"capture"` and rejecting (with a message) anything else.

nodes.body: The self-test flushes the winsys command stream internally and then forces `dirty_hw = 0`, which bypasses `r300_flush_and_cleanup()`. That skips required pre-flush emissions (`r300_emit_hyperz_end`, `r300_emit_query_end`, r500 index bias reset, etc.) and the post-flush state re-dirtying/cleanup (atom dirtying, `vertex_arrays_dirty`, SWTCL unmarking). **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve fill ordering before later GPU reads**

When a valid command stream records `vkCmdFillBuffer` before a later GPU command that reads the buffer (for example filling a vertex/storage buffer, then drawing or dispatching after a barrier), this case skips the fill during `r300vk_replay_gpu`; `r300vk_queue_driver_submit` only runs `r300vk_replay_cpu_readback` after all submitted command buffers have been replayed, flushed, and fenced. The later GPU work therefore consumes the buffer's old contents and the fill is applied too late, producing silent incorrect results for in-order Vulkan command buffers rather than just replacing the former NULL entrypoint crash.

This fill writes only `fb->buffer->resource`, so those coherent persistent maps keep seeing the stale pre-fill bytes until an explicit invalidate copies `bound_resource` back, making `vkCmdFillBuffer` results invisible to valid host-coherent usage.

Placing `**header` after the explicit `type` and `view` means any `type`/`view` keys in `header` will override the CLI-derived values. ```suggestion
    if args.jsonl:
        print(json.dumps({**header, "type": "header", "view": view}, sort_keys=True))
        for item in decoded:
            item = dict(item)
            item.pop("next_index", None)
            print(json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True))
```

The `--view` help text ("gpu=post-reloc absolute VAs") and the comment block above (lines 254-257, "GPU view: absolute VAs") assert the GPU-view value form as absolute VAs, which directly contradicts both the PR description ("The view note is neutral ... does not assert offset-vs-VA") and the deliberately neutral wording in `address_view_note` ("whether the captured value is a BO-relative offset or an absolute VA is capture- and kernel-path-dependent"). Empirically the PR also reports `pre_ib.bin == patched_ib.bin`, falsifying the absolute-VA claim. Consider removing it (or, if the intent was to cover other R300 BO-backed registers actually emitted with `OUT_CS_RELOC` such as `RB3D_AARESOLVE_OFFSET`, `RB3D_COLORPITCH[0-9]+`, `ZB_DEPTHPITCH`, `ZB_ZMASK_OFFSET`, `ZB_HIZ_OFFSET`, or `ZB_ZPASS_ADDR`, extend the regex to those real names instead).

Any error inside `compile_filter` (including unrelated issues like `TypeError` or `SyntaxError` from a bug) will be swallowed and reported as “Invalid filter,” making real failures hard to detect. Please catch only the specific exception types that represent user input errors (or introduce a dedicated `FilterCompileError`) so genuine programming errors still surface normally.

Suggested implementation:

    args.filter_func = None
    if hasattr(args, 'filter') and args.filter:
        try:
            args.filter_func = compile_filter(args.filter)
        except FilterCompileError as e:

```

To fully implement this approach, you should also:

1. Define a dedicated exception type in this module (or a shared module), for example near the top of `src/util/perf/u_trace_compare.py`:

```python
class FilterCompileError(Exception):
    """Raised when a user-provided filter expression is invalid."""
    pass
```

2. Update `compile_filter` to raise `FilterCompileError` for user input errors only. For example:
   - Wrap `SyntaxError` from `compile(...)` in `FilterCompileError`.
   - Wrap any validation logic failures (e.g., disallowed names, invalid AST shapes) in `FilterCompileError`.
   - Avoid catching and wrapping unrelated programming errors (e.g., `NameError` from missing internal variables) so they still propagate.

A sketch inside `compile_filter` might look like:

```python
def compile_filter(expr: str):
    try:
        code = compile(expr, "<filter>", "eval")
    except SyntaxError as e:
        raise FilterCompileError(f"Syntax error in filter: {e}") from e

    # ... perform other validation, and on failure:
    # raise FilterCompileError("...")

    return lambda params: eval(code, {'__builtins__': {}}, {'params': params, **safe_builtins})
```

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the UBO selected by the shader**

When a pipeline layout contains an earlier UBO binding that the shader does not read (for example binding 0 and binding 1 are both UBOs, but the SPIR-V only reads binding 1), `r300vk_nir_remap_single_ubo_to_index0()` still accepts the shader because it sees only one distinct UBO use, but replay then scans the bound sets and binds the first UBO descriptor it finds. That makes the shader read the wrong buffer at CONST[0]; the descriptor set/binding chosen during NIR lowering needs to be retained or layouts with ambiguous earlier UBOs need to be rejected.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle dynamic uniform buffer descriptors**

Layouts using `VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_UNIFORM_BUFFER_DYNAMIC` are accepted elsewhere in this driver and their dynamic offsets are recorded at command time, but this draw-time binder skips them entirely because it only matches plain `UNIFORM_BUFFER`. A shader whose sole UBO is dynamic will compile through the new single-UBO path, then draw without binding its constant buffer (or with stale constants from a previous draw); include dynamic UBOs here and apply the recorded dynamic offset, or reject them before pipeline use.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep graphics and compute descriptor state separate**

This draw path now consumes the single `last_bind_dsets` pointer, but `r300vk_replay_bind_descriptor_sets()` updates that pointer for every bind point and does not filter `bind_point`. In command buffers that bind a compute descriptor set after a graphics descriptor set and then issue another draw, the draw will bind constants from the compute set instead of the last graphics set, so graphics and compute descriptor state need separate replay slots or the draw-side binder must ignore non-graphics binds.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject extra UBO variables before r300 compilation**

This guard only compares the `load_ubo` indices that survived into actual loads, but r300's `ntr_setup_uniforms()` walks all `nir_var_mem_ubo` variables and asserts that there is only one. A SPIR-V module can declare multiple UBO variables while only one is used (or only one survives as a load), which passes this check and then hits the backend assert in debug builds or derives the constant-file size from the wrong remaining variable in release builds; reject multiple UBO variables here or remove dead UBO variables before handing the shader to r300.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

With `robustBufferAccess` advertised, a shader that reads beyond the bound UBO descriptor range must not read bytes past that range, but this path passes the descriptor range straight to r300g without enforcing it. The r300 FS constant upload reads `fs->shader->externals_count` vec4s from `buf->ptr` and does not consult `cb.buffer_size`, so a small `VkDescriptorBufferInfo::range` with a larger declared block can make robust UBO reads consume memory past the descriptor instead of returning safe values or rejecting the pipeline.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Map only the bytes the buffer-image copy can read**

For copies where `bufferRowLength > imageExtent.width`, `src_size = row_pitch * height` includes the padding after the final row even though Vulkan only requires the source buffer to contain bytes through the last copied texel. Because `pipe_buffer_map_range` asserts `offset + length <= buffer->width0` (checked in `src/gallium/auxiliary/util/u_inlines.h`), a valid `vkCmdCopyBufferToImage2` using a padded row layout and a tightly sized source buffer can hit the assertion or fail to map. The size should be based on the last accessed row, e.g. `(height - 1) * row_pitch + width * bpp` for non-empty 2D copies.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject compressed transfer-dst images consistently**

This now accepts `VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT` for every format with any image use, but `r300vk_get_format_properties()` deliberately withholds `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_2_TRANSFER_DST_BIT` for compressed formats because the upload path is texel-addressed and not block-aware. On r300-supported compressed sampled formats, `vkCreateImage` can therefore accept a transfer-dst compressed image that the format properties say is unsupported and that the new copy path cannot address correctly. Mirror the non-compressed gate here before adding `TRANSFER_DST`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run transfer-dst writes before later GPU work**

When a command buffer uploads or clears an image and then draws from it in the same submit, these new transfer-dst commands are skipped during GPU replay and only executed in the post-fence CPU pass, so the draw samples the old image contents and the upload happens too late. `CmdCopyImageToBuffer2` is safe to defer because it is a readback after GPU work, but `CmdCopyBufferToImage2` and `CmdClearColorImage` are producer operations and need to be ordered before subsequent GPU consumers, at least by flushing/replaying the CPU write at the command's position.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Withhold depth/stencil transfer-dst until aspect-aware**

This advertises `TRANSFER_DST` for depth/stencil formats too, but the new upload path ignores `imageSubresource.aspectMask` and copies `util_format_get_blocksize()` bytes per texel as if the buffer contained the full packed pipe format. Valid depth/stencil buffer-image copies, especially stencil-only copies to packed formats such as D24S8, have aspect-specific buffer layouts, so advertising this bit lets applications issue copies that write the wrong bytes into the image. Keep depth/stencil transfer-dst disabled until the replay path handles each aspect separately.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

For valid render passes that use more than one color target, `VkClearAttachment::colorAttachment` selects the subpass color attachment to clear, but the recorded command only keeps the clear value and rect. During replay every `CmdClearAttachments` entry is therefore applied to `current_render_pass->begin_rp.color_image`, i.e. the first color attachment resolved in `CmdBeginRenderPass`, so clearing `colorAttachment = 1` corrupts attachment 0 and leaves attachment 1 unchanged. When `vkCmdClearAttachments` is used for a depth or stencil attachment, this branch records no command at all, so the attachment remains unchanged. That is reachable for valid command buffers because `r300vk_get_format_properties` still advertises `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_2_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_BIT` for supported depth/stencil formats; if depth/stencil clears are not implemented yet, accepting the entrypoint as a silent no-op makes tests that clear depth/stencil inside a render pass render against stale contents.

When a command buffer copies an image and then uses the destination in later GPU work in the same submit, this case makes `r300vk_replay_gpu()` skip the copy, while `r300vk_queue_driver_submit()` only runs `r300vk_replay_cpu_readback()` after all command buffers have been replayed and the GPU fence has completed. When `background` is true, the parent returns immediately at line 403 without ever calling `waitpid()` on the forked child. Previously, `system("... &")` relied on the intermediate shell process to exit so init/PID‑1 could reap the backgrounded `trace-cmd extract`; with a direct `fork()`+`execvp()` the calling process is the direct parent of the long‑running child and it will accumulate as a zombie until the host process exits. This affects the `extract_argv` call site (`gpuvis_trigger_capture_and_keep_tracing`, line 716), which is the only background user today but is invoked once per capture.

Consider either double‑forking (fork an intermediate child that itself forks and `_exit(0)`s, then `waitpid` the intermediate in the parent so the grandchild is reparented to init), or installing a `SIGCHLD` handler / `signal(SIGCHLD, SIG_IGN)` so backgrounded children are auto‑reaped.

If `open(log_path, ...)` fails in the child, the failure is silently swallowed and the child proceeds to `execvp` with the parent's inherited stdout/stderr, which contradicts the caller's intent to redirect output to a log file (and, for the `extract_argv` background call site, will leak `trace-cmd` chatter onto the host program's stdout/stderr). Consider `_exit(127)` on `open` failure, or at minimum redirect to `/dev/null` as a fallback.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reap background trace-cmd children**

When `gpuvis_trigger_capture_and_keep_tracing()` starts `trace-cmd extract` in the background, this helper returns immediately without ever waiting for that direct child. Unlike the previous shell `... &` path where the backgrounded process was reparented away from the Mesa process, each completed extract now remains as a zombie until the application exits (unless the app has explicitly disabled child reaping), so repeated captures can leak process-table entries. Consider reaping these background children asynchronously or double-forking before returning.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retry the foreground wait after EINTR**

When `trace-cmd start/stop/reset` runs in a process that receives an unrelated signal while this `waitpid()` is blocked, `waitpid` can return `-1` with `errno == EINTR`; this path then returns `-1` without reaping the direct child even though the command may have completed successfully. That leaves a zombie and reports a spurious tracing failure in signal-heavy applications, unlike the background branch just above which already retries on `EINTR`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

nodes.body: The new multitap parity gate is described (and commented) as rejecting only when `load_ssbo` count exceeds the reduction-tree tap count, but the code currently rejects on any inequality (`!=`). This narrows admission beyond the stated intent and can reject cases where the same `load_ssbo` def appears multiple times in the add tree (taps > number of load instructions). If the intent is only to reject stray extra loads, gate on `>` to match the PR description and the preceding comment.

nodes.body: The carrier-size guard computes `element_bytes` using `value_bit_size / 8u`, which silently truncates for non-byte-aligned bit sizes (e.g., `value_bit_size==1` yields `element_bytes==0`) and can therefore skip the mismatch rejection even though the kernel store width is not representable by the texel carrier model. It’s safer to explicitly reject non-byte-aligned bit sizes (and avoid repeated `util_format_get_blocksize(fmt)` calls).

nodes.body: `ow` can evaluate to exactly 1.0 for the last block-row when `blocks_total/blocks_per_line` is a half-integer (e.g. CIF example in the description). With the current zscan samplers using `PIPE_TEX_WRAP_REPEAT` for `wrap_t`, a normalized coord of 1.0 will wrap to 0.0 and sample row 0 instead of the last row. Computing the row texcoord using the actual texture row count (ceil(blocks_total/blocks_per_line)) keeps the center-biased coordinate safely in (0, 1) for all rows and avoids REPEAT wraparound.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize centered rows with the aligned texture height**

When `blocks_total` is not divisible by `blocks_per_line`, the source texture is taller than `blocks_total / blocks_per_line` because `vl_mpeg12_decoder.c:179` allocates `align(dec->num_blocks, dec->blocks_per_line) / dec->blocks_per_line` rows. Adding the 0.5 row bias while still dividing by `blocks_total` can push the last partial row to `>= 1.0` (for example a legal macroblock-aligned 1040x16 stream has `blocks_total=520`, `blocks_per_line=32`, so row 16 becomes `16.5*32/520 > 1`), and with `PIPE_TEX_WRAP_REPEAT` that samples the first row instead of the final coefficients. The center coordinate needs to be normalized by the aligned row count, not the unaligned block count.
